identity.method: Exact COL26.8 accepted species usage verified against the pinned search and hierarchy registries, including verbatim name, authorship, rank, sourceDatasetId and every accepted parent node.
identity.scope: Nominal species as represented by COL26.8 usage 3T6ZV. The cited census reports a historical 2014 estimate across seven management units in Rio de Janeiro state; it is not a current abundance estimate or complete species account.

lifeStatusScope.wild: The population evidence is from free-ranging golden lion tamarins surveyed across management units in Atlantic Forest, Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: Domestication has not been assessed; the cited study concerns wild population management and does not provide evidence of domestication.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: Fossil occurrence and geological age have not been assessed.

gaps: No morphology evidence was assessed in this batch.
Reproduction, development, lifespan and other life-history traits have not been assessed.

claims.text: The point-transect-with-lures census estimated 3,706 golden lion tamarins (95% CI 1,863–5,383) in 2014. The authors estimated approximately 59% (2,176) were from remnant wild populations, 34% (1,281) descendants of captive-born reintroduced animals, and 7% (249) descendants of translocated wild groups; these are survey-based historical estimates, not direct counts or current abundance.
claims.locator: Results, paragraph reporting 3,706 individuals and population origins; Table 2; Methods section Censusing GLTs throughout their geographic range
claims.placeTimeScope: Seven management units across golden lion tamarin range in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil; geographic distribution sampled using playback surveys from August 2013 to January 2014; abundance estimate refers to 2014.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild metapopulation estimate includes remnant wild populations, descendants of captive-born reintroduced animals, and descendants of wild translocated groups; no currently captive animals are counted.

gaps: The estimate is specific to the 2014 survey and its seven management-unit design; it does not establish current population size or subsequent trend.
Other ecology, range completeness, demographic rates and independently assessed conservation status were not evaluated in this batch.
No phylogenetic or evolutionary evidence was assessed.
A current or historical range inventory was not assessed; the census sampling extent is not a complete distribution account.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No threat status, trend or range-wide conservation assessment was assessed.

reasons: One field census supplies bounded historical population evidence; other facets remain not-assessed.
The survey is not a current population estimate or a complete species account.
No independent expert review has been completed.
